I am 72 years old, and I have worked these 12 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. My husband passed away ten years ago, and my son is working in the county town, so mostly it is just me in the fields, though I hire my nephew and a few day-laborers at harvest time when I cannot keep up. I have 8 mu of good flat land where I do the wheat-maize rotation, and 4 mu of lighter sandy soil by the well where I grow cotton. I do not change much from last year—last year the harvest was decent, and at my age, changing things is a good way to lose money.

For the winter wheat on the 8 mu, I will sow the improved Jimai variety, about 25 jin of seed per mu. I always run the rotary tiller before planting in October to get a fine seedbed. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base—that is 50 kg per mu, the 15-15-15 kind from the dealer—and then I topdress with urea twice, 30 jin per mu at green-up and again at jointing. That works out to about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium. I irrigate three times: once before the freeze, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. My well has never run dry. I spray twice, once for weeds and once for aphids and rust. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the spring does not turn too dry.

After wheat harvest in early June, I plant summer maize the same day—there is no time to waste. I buy hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu. I run the rotary tiller once quick to chop the wheat stubble, then plant. Base fertilizer is 40 kg of compound per mu, and at the big trumpet stage I spread 40 jin of urea per mu. That is about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Summer rains sometimes help, but I irrigate twice for sure—at jointing and at filling. I spray twice for corn borer and armyworm. A normal year should give me 600 kg per mu.

My 4 mu of cotton goes in the ground in late April when the soil warms. I plant improved Bt cotton seed. Cotton needs more potassium than grain crops—the dealer told me that years ago and he was right—so I put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and I topdress with urea twice during flowering and boll stage. That comes to about 14 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: at flowering, at peak boll, and at boll opening. Even with Bt seed, I spray three times for aphids and red spider mite. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I know some people say fertilizer is too expensive and we should use less, but I have seen what happens when you cut back. Old Li tried saving money two years ago and his wheat turned yellow and thin—he lost more than 100 jin per mu. Fertilizer costs money, but a bad harvest is a disaster. I watch what my neighbors do, and if everyone around me is applying about the same amount, I do the same. At my age, I am not experimenting on my land. I need the crops to come in so I have grain to eat, some cotton to sell for cash, and money for my medicine.
